evidence.observation: get_parser() builds one configargparse.ArgumentParser and wires three input sources onto the same option table: explicit CLI tokens, AIDER_* environment variables (auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_"), and YAML config files (config_file_parser_class=configargparse.YAMLConfigFileParser, default_config_files=default_config_files supplied by the caller). Because all three sources drive one parser, they compete per key, which is the layer where an explicit CLI token can outrank an env/config value.

Inside get_parser the tri-state fixture for this contract is declared: group.add_argument("--attribute-author", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=None, ...) at lines 451-459, so the option is genuinely tri-state (unset None / --attribute-author True / --no-attribute-author False). Its boolean siblings are declared the same way with explicit defaults right above (:--auto-commits default=True, lines 439-444; --dirty-commits default=True, lines 445-450). A BooleanOptionalAction sets the dest directly from the CLI token, so an explicit flag overrides any env/config-derived starting value while an omitted flag keeps the declared default.

The full get_parser body declares 33 argparse.BooleanOptionalAction options, every one with an explicit default (extracted by AST in .prale-eval/demo_boolean_override.py), and the two CLI inputs that select the config/env sources themselves: -c/--config with is_config_file=True (lines 788-797) and --env-file with default=default_env_file(git_root) (lines 800-805). Both are ordinary parsed options, so an explicit CLI value for a boolean key outranks any config-file or environment value for that same key.

default_env_file(git_root) resolves .env at the git root (or ".env" when no root is known) and is used as the default for the --env-file option; it documents that the environment input source has an implicit, replaceable default against which an explicit --env-file CLI value wins.

TestMain.setUp seeds the environment with AIDER_CHECK_UPDATE="false" and AIDER_ANALYTICS="false" (lines 25-26) before driving main(), and isolates HOME/.aider.conf.yml so config/env sources cannot leak between cases. It shows the accepted test harness for asserting input-source precedence in this repository.

test_main_with_git_config_yml writes .aider.conf.yml with auto-commits: false and asserts kwargs["auto_commits"] is False, then rewrites it with auto-commits: true and asserts True. This pins the config-file input source for a boolean key and shows the value reaching Coder.create().

test_main_args exercises explicit CLI tokens for boolean keys in both directions: main(["--no-auto-commits"]) yields auto_commits False while main(["--auto-commits"]) yields True, and an empty argument list yields auto_commits True and dirty_commits True, with main(["--no-dirty-commits"]) yielding dirty_commits False. This is the repository's canonical proof that an explicit CLI flag selects the value and that untouched keys keep their declared defaults.

test_true_vals_in_env_file writes AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=on into .env, runs main() with no CLI flag for that key, and asserts kwargs["show_diffs"] is True, proving the environment input source is consumed when no explicit CLI value is supplied.

test_false_vals_in_env_file writes AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=off and asserts kwargs["show_diffs"] is False, the BooleanOptionalAction counterpart of the previous case; it shows off/on string coercion for the AIDER_* environment layer.

test_load_dotenv_files_override builds oauth-keys.env, git-root .env and a sub-directory .env and asserts the loaded order (oauth first, then git root, then CWD) and that SHARED_VAR resolves to the last loaded file's value. This documents the environment layer's own per-key override order beneath the explicit CLI level.

main() calls get_parser(default_config_files, git_root) and then parser.parse_args(argv) (lines 479-504), threading the resulting namespace into the runtime construction of InputOutput/Coder.create. The value chosen by input-source precedence in get_parser is therefore exactly the value consumed at runtime; no later step re-reads env/config for a boolean key.

claims.claim: The fixture selected for this contract, --attribute-author (dest attribute_author), is declared in get_parser with action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction and default=None, so it is tri-state (unset -> None, --attribute-author -> True, --no-attribute-author -> False); an explicit CLI token therefore sets the value of that key directly, and when no flag is given the declared default None is preserved.

get_parser constructs a single configargparse.ArgumentParser that binds AIDER_* environment variables (auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_") and YAML config files (YAMLConfigFileParser plus default_config_files) onto the same option table as explicit CLI tokens, with -c/--config (is_config_file=True) and --env-file as ordinary CLI options; because the three sources are layered per key, an explicit CLI value overrides an environment or config-file value for the same boolean key.

Overriding one boolean key via the CLI does not change unrelated defaults: the 33 BooleanOptionalAction options each declare an explicit default (e.g. --auto-commits True, --dirty-commits True), so flags the user does not pass keep those declared values even when an env var or config file provides a value for the fixture key.

The repository's own acceptance tests pin the same precedence: test_main_args shows explicit --no-auto-commits/--auto-commits selecting False/True while an empty argv leaves auto_commits and dirty_commits at their declared True defaults; test_main_with_git_config_yml shows a .aider.conf.yml key (auto-commits) selecting the value; and test_true_vals_in_env_file / test_false_vals_in_env_file show AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=on/off selecting show_diffs when no CLI flag is passed. Each case changes a single key without disturbing the others.

main() parses argv once with the parser returned by get_parser and threads the namespace into Coder.create/InputOutput, so the CLI-overridden value is the value actually consumed at runtime and no downstream step re-resolves the key from env or config.

conclusion: The contract holds: for the tri-state boolean fixture --attribute-author (aider/args.py:get_parser, action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=None) an explicit CLI token (--attribute-author / --no-attribute-author) is parsed by the same configargparse option table that binds AIDER_* environment variables and .aider.conf.yml values, so the CLI value overrides an environment or config-file value for that key in either direction. Defaults of the other boolean options are declared explicitly and are left untouched. The executable demo .prale-eval/demo_boolean_override.py statically extracts the real option declarations and parser wiring with AST, reproduces configargparse's documented CLI > env > config-file > default per-key precedence over those real declared defaults, and passed 24 checks (exit 0, 'CONTRACT HOLDS'). Limitation: configargparse and shtab are not installed in this sandbox, so the live parse path could not be executed; per instructions nothing was installed and the limitation is recorded in the validation notes and in .prale-eval/contract-deliverable.md.
